data.narrative:
Astrolight, a seed-stage space & aerospace company founded by Laurynas Mačiulis, has raised €2.8M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 6 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private companies in the Space & Aerospace sector, including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, and Sierra Space.

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using the €2.8M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier for seed-to-next-stage progression yields €7M. The peer-median method could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables (only 1 same-stage peer identified; analysis requires ≥3). Public-comp anchoring was inapplicable because target revenue is not disclosed, and private companies at seed stage rarely report this metric. The public Space & Aerospace sector median P/S multiple stands at 24.6x across the five listed comps, but cannot be leveraged without revenue data.

The triangulated valuation range of €6M–€8M (median €7M) reflects the stage-progression result with modest downside/upside brackets. Key uncertainties include the absence of early-stage revenue traction data, limited comparable seed-stage transactions in the sector, and inherent volatility in space-tech venture valuations. Additional certainty would require disclosed financial metrics or identification of closer-stage private comparables.
